title: Lower a car's glovebox past its stops with a two-handed squeeze, swap the cabin air filter behind it, and close it back past the stops
instruction: Take the glovebox down, replace the cabin air filter behind it with the new one from the table, and put the glovebox back up.
context: New here: the two-handed glovebox removal and refit on most cars. Both side walls must be squeezed in at once (about 10 N each) to drop the glovebox past its sprung stops, then pushed back up until the stops snap behind the dash; in between, the filter must be drawn from and slid into a keyed 200 mm slot reached through the opening. This is a different skill from swapping a filter under a cover. It is a routine service item for automotive service technicians and mechanics (BLS 49-3023, about 680,000 workers) and quick-lube technicians. Keyed or stepped filter frames, like the rib here, are common on OEM filters.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Dashboard section (cropped passenger-side dash, dark grey ABS, fixed to the table; full-size parts, mounted low): 54 cm wide (y -0.27..0.27), 43.5 cm tall, 37 cm deep; its fascia (2 cm thick) faces the robot at x = 0.424, with a glovebox opening 42 cm wide (|y| < 0.21) from 8.5 cm to 40 cm above the table. Glovebox: a moulded polypropylene bin, 0.85 kg, 36 cm wide, its lid 2 cm thick and 21 cm tall, 6 cm deep at the floor and 15.6 cm deep at the top (slanted back wall), hinged along the opening's bottom edge (axis at x = 0.45, 13.5 cm above the table); it swings toward the robot, has a damper (0.25 N m s/rad) and hangs on its hinge stop at 110 degrees when lowered. The upper part of each side wall (above 5 cm) is a flexing panel that can be pushed 14 mm inward against a spring (900 N/m, 2.7 N preload: about 10 N at the 8 mm needed to clear a stop, 15 N at 14 mm); each carries a 54 x 60 mm thumb pad (26 mm proud, 4 mm inside the opening's edge) and, near its back edge, a POM stop bump whose square-faced part, toward the robot, stands 36 mm proud of the wall (6 mm past the opening's edge); behind it a 20-degree chamfer rises from 25 mm to 38.1 mm. At the start the glovebox is open, resting on its stops: both bumps against the rear face of the fascia beside the opening (47.6 degrees open). Behind the opening, 14 cm behind the hinge axis, is the HVAC housing's face (unpainted PP) with the filter slot: 22.25 cm wide (3.75 mm play each side), 3.6 cm tall, its floor 21.7 cm above the table, with a 1.5 cm wide, 9 mm deep key channel in its ceiling 5.75-7.25 cm left of centre; the slot runs 21 cm deep to a back wall, with 45-degree moulded lead-ins at its mouth (a sill from 16 mm below the floor, 10 mm cheeks at both sides, and a 10 mm hood over the outer 4 cm of each side). Cabin air filters (two, same shape): rigid plastic frame with pleated media, 200 mm deep x 215 mm wide x 30 mm thick, 0.15 kg, with a 10 mm wide, 5 mm tall key rib along the top face (6-7 cm left of centre) and a pull tab on the front edge (35 mm long, 16 mm thick, 60 mm tall, standing 30 mm above the frame). The used filter (grey-brown) starts fully in the slot, tab against the housing face. The new filter (white) lies flat on top of a blue upturned plastic parts bin (30 x 26 x 10 cm, fixed) centred at (0.36, -0.45), the filter centred at (0.33, -0.45), tab toward the robot, rib up. The table left of the dash (around (0.30, 0.40)) is clear. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time: the glovebox is forced past a stop it was not squeezed clear of (a bump more than 3 mm into the fascia, i.e. the stop broken), the glovebox is forced more than 3 degrees past its hinge stop, or a filter falls off the table (its centre 5 cm below the table top). Otherwise, at the end: 0.25 if the glovebox has been lowered past both stops (opened 72 degrees or more, at any time); 0.5 if, as well, the old filter is out of the dash section (its whole footprint outside the dash's), resting on the table (lowest point within 1 cm of the table top) and let go; 0.75 if, as well, the new filter is fully in: its front face at most 3 mm proud of the seated position, within 4 mm of the slot's centre line and floor, level and square within 3 degrees, let go. 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): all of that, with the glovebox back up on its stops (within 1.5 degrees of the stop angle or above, both flexing panels sprung back out within 2 mm), every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the glovebox and both filters, and everything still. Let go means every part of both grippers is at least 2 cm from that filter. Putting the old filter back in scores no more than 0.25. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Lower the glovebox (squeeze both side walls), slide the old filter back into the slot rib up until its tab meets the housing, put the new filter back on the parts bin, and swing the glovebox up until both stops click behind the fascia; it then rests on them.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. The dash is a cropped section (no instrument panel above the opening, no door or seat) mounted low on the table so the arms can reach; every handled part is full size. Each glovebox wall's flex is a sprung slide. The filter housing's clip-on access door (fitted on some cars) and the glovebox latch are omitted: the slot is open and the glovebox starts open. Filters are rigid, with no pleat flex, dust or airflow.
